quicktext.options.intro.message: Except for the privacy setting below, all Quicktext settings can be controlled and configured in the Quicktext Manager, alongside your templates and scripts.

quicktext.remoteRequests.label.message: Allow templates to contact remote servers and send data to them (URL tag)

quicktext.remoteRequests.description.message: This setting is turned off by default. While it is off, Quicktext blocks every request made by the URL tag and no data leaves your computer. When you turn it on, a template using the URL tag will contact the web address specified in that template and may send the following data to it, depending on what the template requests: the recipients of the message (To, Cc, Bcc), your sender identity, the subject, the current text selection, the current clipboard content, the names and sizes of the attachments, and the headers and attachment names of the message you are replying to or forwarding. The web address is chosen by the author of the template, not by Quicktext. No data is sent to Quicktext or its authors.

quicktext.remoteBlocked.label.message:
Quicktext blocked a request to “$P1$”.

This template uses the URL tag, which can send data from your message to a remote server. To allow this, enable remote requests in the Quicktext options (Add-ons Manager → Quicktext → Options), where you can also see what is sent.

migration.intro.quote.message: Thank you to all my beta testers for your ongoing support and patience in making this transition possible. Your feedback has been invaluable!

migrationReport.intro.message: Quicktext is now a modern WebExtension. It will stay compatible with future Thunderbird versions without needing an update for each release. As a consequence, it no longer has direct access to the files on your computer and no longer supports the Quicktext v5 script API. The templates, scripts and settings listed below still depend on these features and need your attention.

migrationReport.filesystem.description.message: These templates and scripts reference files on your computer. Such tags are now skipped: the files are no longer inserted or attached, and Quicktext shows a notice in the compose window instead. To fix this, copy the files into a Quicktext storage location and change the tags as suggested below. See the $LINK$ for details.

migrationReport.filesystem.oldVersion.message: Alternatively, install Quicktext $VERSION$ from the $LINK$. It still includes the migration wizard, which copies the files and changes the tags automatically. Run the wizard right after restarting Thunderbird, then update Quicktext again.

migration.incompatible.description.message: These scripts use deprecated Quicktext v5 APIs that are no longer available. They need to be rewritten using the $LINK$.

migration.dropped.intro.message: The following configuration sources relied on direct filesystem access, which is no longer available in modern WebExtensions.

migration.dropped.description.message: If you previously used a local folder to store your templates or to share them across computers, you can install a $VFSLINK$ as a replacement - for example the $WEBDAVLINK$ to store templates on a WebDAV server (ownCloud, Nextcloud, etc.), or the $HOMEFOLDERLINK$ to continue using a folder on your computer.

migration.desc.fileImport.message: This import read templates from a local file on every startup. WebExtensions can no longer directly access the local filesystem.

migration.desc.fileStorage.message: Templates and scripts were read from this local folder. WebExtensions can no longer directly access the local filesystem.
